A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Selective Rotary Position Embedding by the same authors. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, added, and removed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MQAR, MAD, copying, state-tracking, language-modeling, and throughput results in Section 4, with experimental settings in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic-task results and reports revised language-model experiments, including 1.3B-parameter GLA results and additional perplexity evaluations.

M1.justification: The core selective-rotation procedure in Equations 12–13 is retained. V2 Section 4.3 describes switching language-model angle parameterization from queries to L2-normalized inputs and testing rank-8/16 MLPs and post-convolution SiLU, extending v1's phase-gate, bias, and weight-normalization variants.

E1.justification: V2 Table 3 adds the benchmark labeled 'Wiki.' for perplexity evaluation. FineWeb training, MQAR, MAD, copying, S2/A3 state tracking, and the previously reported downstream language tasks remain.

E2.justification: The accuracy comparisons retain NoPE and RoPE across GLA, Gated DeltaNet, and FoX, and the MQAR comparator set is unchanged. However, v1 Figure 5's throughput comparison against RoPE and NoPE disappears. Performer, CosFormer, and ALiBi receive theoretical comparisons rather than new empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: V1's language-model experiments use 370M-parameter models trained on 35B tokens. V2 reports 370M GLA/FoX and approximately 400M Gated DeltaNet at 10B tokens, plus 1.3B GLA at 26B tokens. It also introduces averaged perplexity in the GLA ablation table. Context length, tokenizer, and synthetic-task protocols are retained.

E4.justification: V1 Table 2 evaluates phase gates, bias, and their combination across three language-model architectures. V2 replaces this with a GLA-only SiLU/phase-gate ablation and removes the Triton-versus-PyTorch throughput analysis. MAD component ablations and synthetic length-extrapolation analyses remain.

E5.justification: The copying confidence bands, five state-tracking seeds, and copying seed 42 are retained. V2 adds no new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing for the language-model results.

E6.justification: The 35B-token language-model results are replaced by results under the revised budgets, with added Wiki. perplexities and 1.3B GLA entries. The latter report average accuracies of 55.2 for NoPE, 54.4 for RoPE, and 54.6 for Selective RoPE; these are not same-setting comparisons with v1. Synthetic results remain unchanged, while v1's reported up-to-340% prefill speedup disappears.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.6 derives Performer and CosFormer recurrences and adds Theorem 2 with a proof concerning PRF variance. Expanded Appendix A.7 derives ALiBi's exponential decay and revises FoX's accumulation from products of log-gates to sums. The original RFF, spectral-analysis, and Householder derivations are largely retained.

C1.justification: The central Selective RoPE and rotation-plus-decay contributions persist. V2 drops the abstract's claim of uncovering implicit positional structure in softmax, narrows incorporation from 'any' to 'most' gated linear Transformers, and qualifies the conclusion's language-model downstream benefit as applying to linear-attention variants.

C2.justification: V2 explains that softmax-induced rotations telescope and lack explicit positional bias, although the section summary still describes positional encoding. It withdraws the inference that GLA with Selective RoPE lies outside TC0 and replaces broad MAD/language-model improvement statements with more qualified interpretations, including architecture- and scale-dependent tradeoffs.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation repository link and documents normalized inputs, rank-8/16 MLPs, SiLU, and FoX's output-norm-OFF setting. It removes Appendix B.3's PyTorch class listing and the Triton fusion details. Appendix B.1 now associates the same reported training times with 10B rather than 35B tokens.

R1.justification: Appendices A.6–A.7 substantially expand the relationship to Performer, CosFormer, and ALiBi. The introduction also develops the connection to earlier complex recurrent models and adds François et al. (2025). References associated with the removed spectral-bias, throughput, and Chinchilla discussions disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, numerous background and design-principle paragraphs, and language-model discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Appendix organization changes through the new kernel-comparison section, expanded ALiBi/FoX subsections, and removal of the implementation subsection, while the main section order remains.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from four dot-spectrum diagrams to three annotated query-key vector panels. V1's throughput figure, gate-spectrum table, and code figure are removed. V2 separates language-model results from ablations, adds the Wiki. column and kernel-transition table, and relocates retained synthetic figures.

improvement.justification: V2 usefully withdraws the TC0 inference, qualifies empirical benefits, and develops additional theoretical connections and larger-model tradeoffs. However, it removes throughput evidence and broad component ablations while retaining the low-cost claim. Its FoX averages are also unexplained: Table 3's NoPE accuracies average approximately 46.18%, whereas Avg. reports 45.3%. These gains and losses leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
